title: Shared body, different heads
caption: The frozen encoder turns frame 0 into 256 tokens x 384 numbers. A 4-block transformer reads them, with the time t setting each block's scale and shift. FrameNet's head outputs one arrow and walks along the sphere. RotNet's heads output a unit direction and an angle, then rotate. Each has its own loss. GIF

title: Walking on the sphere (the exp map)
caption: The head's arrow lies flat on the sphere at the first frame. The guess is where you land after walking that far along the surface in that direction. The error is the angle to the true frame. RotNet picks the walking distance first (the orange ring of points that far away), then the direction. GIF

title: Same guess, two ways to grade it
caption: Left: FrameNet outputs one arrow and gets one score, so a miss can't be split into 'too far' and 'wrong way'. Right: RotNet outputs a distance (orange ring) and a unit direction (purple arrow), graded separately. Handing it the true direction leaves only the small distance error. GIF

title: Right distance, wrong direction
caption: Even with the distance exactly right, a guess more than 60° off lands further from the truth than not moving at all (freeze). On new clips both models are about 82° off; on training clips RotNet is about 26° off. Idealised: the real RotNet also overshoots the distance on new clips (17.6° vs 13.6°). GIF
